title: Switches - CS / IOS XE software versions IOS XE 26.1.1 changelog

announcements.post_subject: A new Beta CS Switch firmware is now available

Important notes: After upgrading to Cloud Management with IOS XE, it is not possible to downgrade to any CS firmware via Dashboard. In order to downgrade to CS firmware, a factory reset may be required, and support assistance will be necessary. Please consider this before upgrading your network to Cloud Management with IOS XE. Learn more - http://cs.co/9002xhAan

Please refer to the documentation to review upgrade/migration checklist and key considerations: https://documentation.meraki.com/Switching/Cloud_Management_with_IOS_XE/Product_Information/Overviews_and_Datasheets/Cloud_Management_with_IOS_XE_Overview#Before_You_Upgrade_or_Migrate:_Key_Considerations

Please review the list of supported models with minimum firmware support versions (http://cs.co/90017Wj55) before proceeding with the upgrade. Attempting to convert unsupported models may result in an unusable switch.

Stacking Limit for C9200L: C9200L series models support stacking configurations of up to 5 members. Please ensure your stacks for these models adhere to this limit. Exceeding 5 members may lead to unexpected behavior. This will be resolved in a future release.

Switch Templates with bound networks cannot directly upgrade from CS firmware to IOS XE firmware. We recommend unbinding and migrating networks to IOS XE independently, and then rebinding into an IOS XE switch template. Please see this article for details: https://documentation.meraki.com/Switching/Cloud_Management_with_IOS_XE/Product_Information/Overviews_and_Datasheets/Cloud_Management_with_IOS_XE_Overview#Migrating_a_Switch_Template

After upgrading from CS to IOS XE, ensure the upgrade process has fully completed before making any configuration changes or rebooting the switch. To confirm that it is safe to proceed, review the event log for successful completion messages or view the firmware upgrade completion status on the switch details page. Making changes or rebooting before the upgrade is complete may result in switchports reverting to their default configuration
Client tracking is automatically enabled on switchports configured as access ports and rated for 10Gbps and below.
Cloud management with ios xe overview: The new 26.1 release brings cloud management to more switch platforms, including the C9200, C9300, and C9500 high performance, and the IE3500 families. It also unlocks more powerful IOS XE features like advanced routing, high availability, and expanded cloud-powered value, so you can manage a seamless, secure, and scalable network from access to core, all within one intuitive dashboard.
CS17 or IOS-XE 17.15+ are prerequisite firmware requirements before initiating an upgrade to cloud management with IOS XE 26.1.1.
Release highlights: In this release, we are excited to introduce several new enhancements and optimizations focused on improving performance, reliability, and user experience. The key highlights include:

This release addresses a wide range of issues impacting dashboard connectivity, device configuration synchronization, and stack stability. These fixes contribute to a more robust platform and smoother operations.
UAC now leverages both FED-based VLAN discovery and IP Device Tracking data to identify active VLANs, improving the detection of low-traffic links.
Extending cloud management to rugged outdoor networks with the new IE3500 support. http://cs.co/9000B648FG
Expanded Meraki regional cloud support for switches on IOS XE firmware: Cloud Management with IOS XE now available in Meraki India, China, and Canada regions.

Feature Parity between C9350 and C9300: BGP, VRF, Rapid Per-VLAN STP (RPVST+), Routed Ports, Digital Optical Monitoring, Radius Caching, Intelligent Capture Scheduling, SmartPorts, UAC fall back, UAC allow list, and VLAN to SGT mapping.

Added support for STP Portfast. See the Spanning Tree documentation for more information: https://documentation.meraki.com/Switching/MS_-_Switches/Design_and_Configure/Configuration_Guides/Port_and_VLAN_Configuration/Configuring_Spanning_Tree_on_Meraki_Switches_(MS)
Before you upgrade or migrate: key consi: Please refer to the documentation to review key considerations: https://documentation.meraki.com/Switching/Cloud_Management_with_IOS_XE/Product_Information/Overviews_and_Datasheets/Cloud_Management_with_IOS_XE_Overview#Before_You_Upgrade_or_Migrate:_Key_Considerations

Please refer to the documentation to familiarize yourself with management interface architecture changes. https://documentation.meraki.com/MS/Cloud-Native_IOS_XE/Cloud-Native_IOS_XE_Overview#Changes_in_Behavior

For guidance with migrating L3 switches from CS to IOS XE firmware please refer to the detailed guidance here: https://documentation.meraki.com/Switching/Cloud_Management_with_IOS_XE/Install_and_Get_Started/Migrating_Switches_From_CS_Firmware_to_IOS_XE_Firmware?mt-draft=true

After migrating CLI/DNA managed switches to cloud configuration source, please note that console and SSH access are no longer available. All management access is only available via the Dashboard or the local status page through the rear management port/front panel port.
Downgrades from Cloud Management with IOS XE to any prior CS firmware via the Dashboard is restricted.

Catalyst devices need ICMP ping connectivity to several destinations to test uplink connectivity to the dashboard. For successful upgrades and continued connectivity post-upgrade, ensure that outbound ICMP pings from Catalyst devices are permitted to the following destinations: config-2037.meraki.com, catalyst.meraki.com, google.com, 8.8.8.8 (Google DNS) and 2001:4860:4860::8888 (Google DNS).

To ensure a successful upgrade and continued connectivity post-upgrade, resolve before the upgrade all alerts on the Organization > Alerts page that are associated with the switches being upgraded. Resolve “Bad IP assignment” and “VLAN mismatch” alerts on the uplink interfaces, and stacking related alerts such as “Misconfigured Switch”, “Unconfigured Switch” and “Switch Not Connected to Stack” to ensure a successful upgrade.

Layer 3 switches cannot run DHCP servers on uplink interfaces with IOS XE 17.15+. Post-upgrade, Interfaces with both Preferred Uplink and DHCP server configurations will have the DHCP server configuration disabled on that interface.

Switches using the Alternative Management Interface (AMI) will require an L3 SVI to be configured for the same VLAN assigned to AMI. For AMI to work, your network must have AMI configured and your switch must have an SVI configured matching that AMI VLAN.
After upgrading from CS to Cloud Management with IOS XE firmware, port mirroring configurations on module ports will not be retained. Reconfigure port mirroring on module ports following the upgrade.

Cloud-born Catalyst switches (-M) require Meraki licenses, with a 30-day grace period for onboarding to the Meraki Dashboard. Eligible migrated switches can use existing DNA licenses for cloud management until February 1, 2029 - no additional license migration or transfer required. Learn more: http://cs.co/9004hmri2

UDLD now uses Cisco UDLD Aggressive mode on fiber ports and will not be enabled on copper interfaces. Please see https://documentation.meraki.com/Switching/MS_-_Switches/Operate_and_Maintain/How-Tos/Unidirectional_Link_Detection_(UDLD) for more details

Please note: this is the second IOS XE release for C9350 series switch. Support has been added for many advanced layer 3 features, including: BGP, VRF, Rapid Per-VLAN STP (RPVST+), Routed Ports, Digital Optical Monitoring, Radius Caching, Intelligent Capture Scheduling, SmartPorts, UAC fall back, UAC allow list, and VLAN to SGT mapping.

Please note, this is the first IOS XE release for IE-3500 series switch. These advanced layer 3 features are currently not supported: BGP, VRF, Rapid Per-VLAN STP (RPVST+), Routed Ports, Loopback, VRRP, User-defined ACLs on VLAN, SmartPort, Encrypted Traffic Analytics (ETA), Detailed Traffic Analytics (on trunk ports, port channels, and uplink modules). In addition, IE-3500 expansion modules aren't supported at this time.

Storm Control behavior differs between different generations of switches. Please see https://documentation.meraki.com/Switching/MS_-_Switches/Operate_and_Maintain/How-Tos/Storm_Control_for_MS for more details.
Known issues in 26.1.1: In the Local Status Page, you are able to change the configuration of the Uplink Interface to be in the Mgmt-vrf. Mgmt-vrf is not supported in XE 26.1.1 and will be enabled in a future release.

50 Gigabit Ethernet interfaces are not fully supported in this release. Certain functionality on these interfaces is not available, such as the ability to reset a port and to retrieve live port information (such as Spanning Tree blocked state).
The Beacon LED functionality is not available on the C9300LM in this release.

Packet captures on member ports of an aggregate (port channel) are not supported on C9350 and other Silicon One based devices. As a result, the packet capture in Dashboard has been altered to no longer allow member interfaces to be selected. Instead, aggregate (port-channel) interfaces are now allowed to be selected as the source of a packet capture.

In a very rare case scenario during switch boot-up, when the preferred link is down and a specific race condition is met between preferred link coming back up and connectivity to cloud being established, C9200L switches in a stack may temporarily experience a configuration application failure. The system will automatically recover and apply the configuration within 2 hours.
In this release, the C9200L supports a maximum of 128 Layer 3 Interfaces (SVIs). Failures may occur if you attempt to configure more than 128 SVIs.

C9350 switches will not upgrade to 26.1.1. If a network containing C9350 switches upgrades to 26.1.1, the 9350s will instead install or remain on 17.18.2. An updated 26.1.1 release supporting 9350 will be released soon.
Fixed issues in 26.1.1: An active switch running Catalyst 9300 series could experience a segmentation fault in the Inline Power process, resulting in an unexpected reload. This issue has been resolved.
In a 4-member stack configuration, linux_iosd could crash due to memory fragmentation triggered by excessive Spanning Tree Topology Change Notifications (TCNs). This issue has been resolved.
Under certain timing conditions, a 5-member Catalyst 9350 stack could experience a stacking failure following a memory crash related to STP TCN storms. This issue has been resolved.
A Catalyst 9500H device could crash due to a critical meraki_mgrd process failure during uplink selection immediately after bootup. This issue has been resolved.

On platforms using Cisco's Binos SSL stack, a crash could occur at OPENSSL_sk_pop_free during iosd process teardown, particularly in environments with FIPS or OQS provider configurations. This issue has been resolved.
A SELinux violation involving install_cur_trans_log could cause image activate and abort operations to fail during the installation process. This issue has been resolved.

A data inconsistency error (DATACORRUPTION-1-DATAINCONSISTENCY) could be triggered during debug bundle generation or Netconf SSH techsupport collection, potentially interrupting the operation. This issue has been resolved.
A critical process crash on the forwarding processor (fp_0_0, rc=139) could occur during regression or sustained traffic runs on Catalyst 9350 platforms. This issue has been resolved.
A Catalyst 9300 device could fail to complete an image upgrade when using image_label.conf to load an image from ROMMON. This issue has been resolved.
Following an upgrade to a 26.1.1 build, the NextTunnel (NT) connection to the Meraki dashboard could fail to come up. This issue has been resolved.
A SELinux policy violation could cause image download and installation to fail when an upgrade was triggered from the Meraki dashboard. This issue has been resolved.

On devices configured with dual-stack (IPv4 and IPv6) uplink connectivity, image upgrade initiated from the Meraki dashboard could fail because the download defaulted to an IPv6 address without falling back to IPv4. This issue has been resolved.
A bulk configuration apply failure reporting "application communication failure" could occur on Catalyst 9500 series devices, preventing successful provisioning. This issue has been resolved.
After a software image upgrade, uplink connectivity could be lost if route configuration was not correctly preserved across the upgrade. This issue has been resolved.
NextTunnel connectivity could go down after cloud server-related routes were pushed to the device, incorrectly triggering a UAC uplink re-evaluation. This issue has been resolved.

NextTunnel connectivity could be lost following a configuration push from the Meraki dashboard, caused by an ACL-related failure in the forwarding plane during the update. This issue has been resolved.
In a binary (non-cloud) deployment, the UAC preferred uplink interface could be ignored and remain unused even when the interface was active and available. This issue has been resolved.
UAC uplink detection with Device Tracking enabled could take in excess of 3 hours, causing extended periods where cloud management connectivity was unavailable. This issue has been resolved.
When a more specific route was added within the same subnet as the configured gateway, UAC could incorrectly change the gateway IP, causing loss of uplink connectivity. This issue has been resolved.
On MS390 devices, a parser error related to et-analytics configuration could cause the peer device to reload due to a configuration mismatch during HA synchronization. This issue has been resolved.
On Catalyst 9200L, the confd process could leak memory during repeated configuration apply operations, eventually causing the system to reload. This issue has been resolved.

In a Catalyst 9000 stack, if the startup_config_feature_enabled file was not synchronized across all stack members, a device could incorrectly boot using Day 0 configuration instead of the saved startup configuration. This issue has been resolved.
Applying an undebug command within one parser view could unintentionally modify the debug state of a separate, unrelated parser view. This issue has been resolved.
On Catalyst 9200CX platforms, CDP neighbor discovery and basic Layer 2 forwarding could stop functioning after upgrading to certain 26.1.1 builds. This issue has been resolved.
Following a 360-degree switchover combined with an active switch OIR event on a Catalyst 9350, the Power Supply unit could disappear from the output of show inventory. This issue has been resolved.
A GLC-T SFP transceiver on Catalyst 9350 platforms could generate a false link-up notification, causing incorrect port state reporting. This issue has been resolved.

A Catalyst 9350-48HX could incorrectly report the SFP media type for 10G interfaces, resulting in inaccurate hardware inventory information visible to management systems and the Meraki dashboard. This issue has been resolved.
On Catalyst 9200CX, an uplink port optic could fail to be detected following an upgrade, rendering the physical uplink unusable. This issue has been resolved.

Authentication functionality could be completely broken on 26.1.1 images due to a conflict introduced by an encryption feature commit affecting FIPS mode behavior on Meraki-managed platforms. This issue has been resolved.

When a peer device reloaded, an EtherChannel member port could enter a suspended state due to a DAI (Dynamic ARP Inspection) trust state mismatch across the channel members. This issue has been resolved.
A CLI session could hang indefinitely when executing show ip http server or related HTTP server commands on Meraki-managed devices. This issue has been resolved.
The ping command using explicit egress interface and next-hop arguments could fail on Catalyst 9350 platforms running in Meraki-managed mode. This issue has been resolved.
Converting a port from trunk mode to a Layer 3 routed port via the Meraki dashboard could fail with an RPC error, leaving the port in an inconsistent state. This issue has been resolved.

A device could fail to download a YAML manifest document from the Meraki dashboard's generate YAML API due to a TLS handshake failure related to mutual TLS certificate handling. This issue has been resolved.
A traceback could be seen at __be_network_rf_send_swif_event_to_standby_hot following an HA switchover, caused by a regression introduced in a prior release. This issue has been resolved.
On Catalyst 9350, an LSP port could become unreachable when multiple default routes were present, due to a lack of support for local policy route-map on the S1 platform. This issue has been resolved.

When RPVST+ was enabled via the Meraki dashboard on a Catalyst 9350, the spanning tree topology could fail to converge correctly due to an issue with L2-LPTS entry handling. This issue has been resolved.
EAP-TLS authentication could fail for RADIUS traffic over IPv6 on Meraki-managed devices. This issue has been resolved.

On the Meraki dashboard Routing & DHCP page, non-uplink Layer 3 interfaces could not be modified, returning the error "Default Gateway can only be set if the interface is designated as the V4 uplink." This issue has been resolved.
Share your post-upgrade feedback!: We value your feedback on our latest release! Please take a moment to complete this brief 5-minute survey (https://forms.office.com/r/eyh1BZWMZq) and share your experience with us.
Supported models: Note: Breakout Cables aren’t supported at this time.
Transitioning from cs to ios xe 26.1: un: The following CS features are not supported in this release:
Certain features will be added to the IOS XE versions in future releases. Refer to the Cloud Management with IOS XE documentation for further details: http://cs.co/9001Q4ALF

Switches - CS / IOS XE software versions IOS XE 26.1.1 changelog

Important notes

  • After upgrading to Cloud Management with IOS XE, it is not possible to downgrade to any CS firmware via Dashboard. In order to downgrade to CS firmware, a factory reset may be required, and support assistance will be necessary. Please consider this before upgrading your network to Cloud Management with IOS XE. Learn more - http://cs.co/9002xhAan

  • Please refer to the documentation to review upgrade/migration checklist and key considerations: https://documentation.meraki.com/Switching/Cloud_Management_with_IOS_XE/Product_Information/Overviews_and_Datasheets/Cloud_Management_with_IOS_XE_Overview#Before_You_Upgrade_or_Migrate:_Key_Considerations

  • Please review the list of supported models with minimum firmware support versions (http://cs.co/90017Wj55) before proceeding with the upgrade. Attempting to convert unsupported models may result in an unusable switch.

  • Stacking Limit for C9200L: C9200L series models support stacking configurations of up to 5 members. Please ensure your stacks for these models adhere to this limit. Exceeding 5 members may lead to unexpected behavior. This will be resolved in a future release.

  • Switch Templates with bound networks cannot directly upgrade from CS firmware to IOS XE firmware. We recommend unbinding and migrating networks to IOS XE independently, and then rebinding into an IOS XE switch template. Please see this article for details: https://documentation.meraki.com/Switching/Cloud_Management_with_IOS_XE/Product_Information/Overviews_and_Datasheets/Cloud_Management_with_IOS_XE_Overview#Migrating_a_Switch_Template

  • After upgrading from CS to IOS XE, ensure the upgrade process has fully completed before making any configuration changes or rebooting the switch. To confirm that it is safe to proceed, review the event log for successful completion messages or view the firmware upgrade completion status on the switch details page. Making changes or rebooting before the upgrade is complete may result in switchports reverting to their default configuration

  • Client tracking is automatically enabled on switchports configured as access ports and rated for 10Gbps and below.

Cloud management with ios xe overview

  • The new 26.1 release brings cloud management to more switch platforms, including the C9200, C9300, and C9500 high performance, and the IE3500 families. It also unlocks more powerful IOS XE features like advanced routing, high availability, and expanded cloud-powered value, so you can manage a seamless, secure, and scalable network from access to core, all within one intuitive dashboard.

  • CS17 or IOS-XE 17.15+ are prerequisite firmware requirements before initiating an upgrade to cloud management with IOS XE 26.1.1.

Release highlights

  • In this release, we are excited to introduce several new enhancements and optimizations focused on improving performance, reliability, and user experience. The key highlights include:

  • Stability and Reliability Improvements

  • This release addresses a wide range of issues impacting dashboard connectivity, device configuration synchronization, and stack stability. These fixes contribute to a more robust platform and smoother operations.

  • Uplink Auto-Configuration (UAC) Enhancements:

  • UAC now leverages both FED-based VLAN discovery and IP Device Tracking data to identify active VLANs, improving the detection of low-traffic links.

  • Extending cloud management to rugged outdoor networks with the new IE3500 support. http://cs.co/9000B648FG

  • Expanded Meraki regional cloud support for switches on IOS XE firmware: Cloud Management with IOS XE now available in Meraki India, China, and Canada regions.

  • Feature Parity between C9350 and C9300: BGP, VRF, Rapid Per-VLAN STP (RPVST+), Routed Ports, Digital Optical Monitoring, Radius Caching, Intelligent Capture Scheduling, SmartPorts, UAC fall back, UAC allow list, and VLAN to SGT mapping.

  • Added support for STP Portfast. See the Spanning Tree documentation for more information: https://documentation.meraki.com/Switching/MS_-_Switches/Design_and_Configure/Configuration_Guides/Port_and_VLAN_Configuration/Configuring_Spanning_Tree_on_Meraki_Switches_(MS)

Before you upgrade or migrate: key considerations

  • Please refer to the documentation to review key considerations: https://documentation.meraki.com/Switching/Cloud_Management_with_IOS_XE/Product_Information/Overviews_and_Datasheets/Cloud_Management_with_IOS_XE_Overview#Before_You_Upgrade_or_Migrate:_Key_Considerations

  • Please refer to the documentation to familiarize yourself with management interface architecture changes. https://documentation.meraki.com/MS/Cloud-Native_IOS_XE/Cloud-Native_IOS_XE_Overview#Changes_in_Behavior

  • For guidance with migrating L3 switches from CS to IOS XE firmware please refer to the detailed guidance here: https://documentation.meraki.com/Switching/Cloud_Management_with_IOS_XE/Install_and_Get_Started/Migrating_Switches_From_CS_Firmware_to_IOS_XE_Firmware?mt-draft=true

  • After migrating CLI/DNA managed switches to cloud configuration source, please note that console and SSH access are no longer available. All management access is only available via the Dashboard or the local status page through the rear management port/front panel port.

  • Downgrades from Cloud Management with IOS XE to any prior CS firmware via the Dashboard is restricted.

  • Catalyst devices need ICMP ping connectivity to several destinations to test uplink connectivity to the dashboard. For successful upgrades and continued connectivity post-upgrade, ensure that outbound ICMP pings from Catalyst devices are permitted to the following destinations: config-2037.meraki.com, catalyst.meraki.com, google.com, 8.8.8.8 (Google DNS) and 2001:4860:4860::8888 (Google DNS).

  • To ensure a successful upgrade and continued connectivity post-upgrade, resolve before the upgrade all alerts on the Organization > Alerts page that are associated with the switches being upgraded. Resolve “Bad IP assignment” and “VLAN mismatch” alerts on the uplink interfaces, and stacking related alerts such as “Misconfigured Switch”, “Unconfigured Switch” and “Switch Not Connected to Stack” to ensure a successful upgrade.

  • Layer 3 switches cannot run DHCP servers on uplink interfaces with IOS XE 17.15+. Post-upgrade, Interfaces with both Preferred Uplink and DHCP server configurations will have the DHCP server configuration disabled on that interface.

  • Switches using the Alternative Management Interface (AMI) will require an L3 SVI to be configured for the same VLAN assigned to AMI. For AMI to work, your network must have AMI configured and your switch must have an SVI configured matching that AMI VLAN.

  • After upgrading from CS to Cloud Management with IOS XE firmware, port mirroring configurations on module ports will not be retained. Reconfigure port mirroring on module ports following the upgrade.

  • Cloud-born Catalyst switches (-M) require Meraki licenses, with a 30-day grace period for onboarding to the Meraki Dashboard. Eligible migrated switches can use existing DNA licenses for cloud management until February 1, 2029 - no additional license migration or transfer required. Learn more: http://cs.co/9004hmri2

  • UDLD now uses Cisco UDLD Aggressive mode on fiber ports and will not be enabled on copper interfaces. Please see https://documentation.meraki.com/Switching/MS_-_Switches/Operate_and_Maintain/How-Tos/Unidirectional_Link_Detection_(UDLD) for more details

  • Please note: this is the second IOS XE release for C9350 series switch. Support has been added for many advanced layer 3 features, including: BGP, VRF, Rapid Per-VLAN STP (RPVST+), Routed Ports, Digital Optical Monitoring, Radius Caching, Intelligent Capture Scheduling, SmartPorts, UAC fall back, UAC allow list, and VLAN to SGT mapping.

  • Please note, this is the first IOS XE release for IE-3500 series switch. These advanced layer 3 features are currently not supported: BGP, VRF, Rapid Per-VLAN STP (RPVST+), Routed Ports, Loopback, VRRP, User-defined ACLs on VLAN, SmartPort, Encrypted Traffic Analytics (ETA), Detailed Traffic Analytics (on trunk ports, port channels, and uplink modules). In addition, IE-3500 expansion modules aren't supported at this time.

  • Storm Control behavior differs between different generations of switches. Please see https://documentation.meraki.com/Switching/MS_-_Switches/Operate_and_Maintain/How-Tos/Storm_Control_for_MS for more details.

Known issues in 26.1.1

  • In the Local Status Page, you are able to change the configuration of the Uplink Interface to be in the Mgmt-vrf. Mgmt-vrf is not supported in XE 26.1.1 and will be enabled in a future release.

  • 50 Gigabit Ethernet interfaces are not fully supported in this release. Certain functionality on these interfaces is not available, such as the ability to reset a port and to retrieve live port information (such as Spanning Tree blocked state).

  • The Beacon LED functionality is not available on the C9300LM in this release.

  • Packet captures on member ports of an aggregate (port channel) are not supported on C9350 and other Silicon One based devices. As a result, the packet capture in Dashboard has been altered to no longer allow member interfaces to be selected. Instead, aggregate (port-channel) interfaces are now allowed to be selected as the source of a packet capture.

  • In a very rare case scenario during switch boot-up, when the preferred link is down and a specific race condition is met between preferred link coming back up and connectivity to cloud being established, C9200L switches in a stack may temporarily experience a configuration application failure. The system will automatically recover and apply the configuration within 2 hours.

  • In this release, the C9200L supports a maximum of 128 Layer 3 Interfaces (SVIs). Failures may occur if you attempt to configure more than 128 SVIs.

  • C9350 switches will not upgrade to 26.1.1. If a network containing C9350 switches upgrades to 26.1.1, the 9350s will instead install or remain on 17.18.2. An updated 26.1.1 release supporting 9350 will be released soon.

Fixed issues in 26.1.1

  • An active switch running Catalyst 9300 series could experience a segmentation fault in the Inline Power process, resulting in an unexpected reload. This issue has been resolved.

  • In a 4-member stack configuration, linux_iosd could crash due to memory fragmentation triggered by excessive Spanning Tree Topology Change Notifications (TCNs). This issue has been resolved.

  • Under certain timing conditions, a 5-member Catalyst 9350 stack could experience a stacking failure following a memory crash related to STP TCN storms. This issue has been resolved.

  • A Catalyst 9500H device could crash due to a critical meraki_mgrd process failure during uplink selection immediately after bootup. This issue has been resolved.

  • On platforms using Cisco's Binos SSL stack, a crash could occur at OPENSSL_sk_pop_free during iosd process teardown, particularly in environments with FIPS or OQS provider configurations. This issue has been resolved.

  • A SELinux violation involving install_cur_trans_log could cause image activate and abort operations to fail during the installation process. This issue has been resolved.

  • A data inconsistency error (DATACORRUPTION-1-DATAINCONSISTENCY) could be triggered during debug bundle generation or Netconf SSH techsupport collection, potentially interrupting the operation. This issue has been resolved.

  • A critical process crash on the forwarding processor (fp_0_0, rc=139) could occur during regression or sustained traffic runs on Catalyst 9350 platforms. This issue has been resolved.

  • A Catalyst 9300 device could fail to complete an image upgrade when using image_label.conf to load an image from ROMMON. This issue has been resolved.

  • Following an upgrade to a 26.1.1 build, the NextTunnel (NT) connection to the Meraki dashboard could fail to come up. This issue has been resolved.

  • A SELinux policy violation could cause image download and installation to fail when an upgrade was triggered from the Meraki dashboard. This issue has been resolved.

  • On devices configured with dual-stack (IPv4 and IPv6) uplink connectivity, image upgrade initiated from the Meraki dashboard could fail because the download defaulted to an IPv6 address without falling back to IPv4. This issue has been resolved.

  • A bulk configuration apply failure reporting "application communication failure" could occur on Catalyst 9500 series devices, preventing successful provisioning. This issue has been resolved.

  • After a software image upgrade, uplink connectivity could be lost if route configuration was not correctly preserved across the upgrade. This issue has been resolved.

  • NextTunnel connectivity could go down after cloud server-related routes were pushed to the device, incorrectly triggering a UAC uplink re-evaluation. This issue has been resolved.

  • NextTunnel connectivity could be lost following a configuration push from the Meraki dashboard, caused by an ACL-related failure in the forwarding plane during the update. This issue has been resolved.

  • In a binary (non-cloud) deployment, the UAC preferred uplink interface could be ignored and remain unused even when the interface was active and available. This issue has been resolved.

  • UAC uplink detection with Device Tracking enabled could take in excess of 3 hours, causing extended periods where cloud management connectivity was unavailable. This issue has been resolved.

  • When a more specific route was added within the same subnet as the configured gateway, UAC could incorrectly change the gateway IP, causing loss of uplink connectivity. This issue has been resolved.

  • On MS390 devices, a parser error related to et-analytics configuration could cause the peer device to reload due to a configuration mismatch during HA synchronization. This issue has been resolved.

  • On Catalyst 9200L, the confd process could leak memory during repeated configuration apply operations, eventually causing the system to reload. This issue has been resolved.

  • In a Catalyst 9000 stack, if the startup_config_feature_enabled file was not synchronized across all stack members, a device could incorrectly boot using Day 0 configuration instead of the saved startup configuration. This issue has been resolved.

  • Applying an undebug command within one parser view could unintentionally modify the debug state of a separate, unrelated parser view. This issue has been resolved.

  • On Catalyst 9200CX platforms, CDP neighbor discovery and basic Layer 2 forwarding could stop functioning after upgrading to certain 26.1.1 builds. This issue has been resolved.

  • Following a 360-degree switchover combined with an active switch OIR event on a Catalyst 9350, the Power Supply unit could disappear from the output of show inventory. This issue has been resolved.

  • A GLC-T SFP transceiver on Catalyst 9350 platforms could generate a false link-up notification, causing incorrect port state reporting. This issue has been resolved.

  • A Catalyst 9350-48HX could incorrectly report the SFP media type for 10G interfaces, resulting in inaccurate hardware inventory information visible to management systems and the Meraki dashboard. This issue has been resolved.

  • On Catalyst 9200CX, an uplink port optic could fail to be detected following an upgrade, rendering the physical uplink unusable. This issue has been resolved.

  • Authentication functionality could be completely broken on 26.1.1 images due to a conflict introduced by an encryption feature commit affecting FIPS mode behavior on Meraki-managed platforms. This issue has been resolved.

  • When a peer device reloaded, an EtherChannel member port could enter a suspended state due to a DAI (Dynamic ARP Inspection) trust state mismatch across the channel members. This issue has been resolved.

  • A CLI session could hang indefinitely when executing show ip http server or related HTTP server commands on Meraki-managed devices. This issue has been resolved.

  • The ping command using explicit egress interface and next-hop arguments could fail on Catalyst 9350 platforms running in Meraki-managed mode. This issue has been resolved.

  • Converting a port from trunk mode to a Layer 3 routed port via the Meraki dashboard could fail with an RPC error, leaving the port in an inconsistent state. This issue has been resolved.

  • A device could fail to download a YAML manifest document from the Meraki dashboard's generate YAML API due to a TLS handshake failure related to mutual TLS certificate handling. This issue has been resolved.

  • A traceback could be seen at __be_network_rf_send_swif_event_to_standby_hot following an HA switchover, caused by a regression introduced in a prior release. This issue has been resolved.

  • On Catalyst 9350, an LSP port could become unreachable when multiple default routes were present, due to a lack of support for local policy route-map on the S1 platform. This issue has been resolved.

  • When RPVST+ was enabled via the Meraki dashboard on a Catalyst 9350, the spanning tree topology could fail to converge correctly due to an issue with L2-LPTS entry handling. This issue has been resolved.

  • EAP-TLS authentication could fail for RADIUS traffic over IPv6 on Meraki-managed devices. This issue has been resolved.

  • On the Meraki dashboard Routing & DHCP page, non-uplink Layer 3 interfaces could not be modified, returning the error "Default Gateway can only be set if the interface is designated as the V4 uplink." This issue has been resolved.
